newsitem.title: KENYA: Foreign investors boost Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investors boost Nairobi bourse.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index picked up 6.25 points to 3522.82 on Thursday boosted by foreign investors, bourse officials said.
Turnover was posted at 45.221 million shillings on 2,397,639 shares from 34.206 million shillings on 541,061 shares.

Foreign investors traded two million shillings of Kenya Airways at a reserve price of 9.0 from 8.80 on the three-day special board; 70,000 shares of Lonrho Motors EA changed hands at 125 from 128; and 30,000 shares of Kenya Power & Lighting at 125 from 126 on the one-hour-hold special board.
Foreign investors have dominated trading at the Nairobi bourse this month. Their demand for selected shares in the market has pushed those shares upwards.

Brokers said as a result many small investors who could not afford to keep their money in shares for the long term were speculating heavily on foreign-supported shares, hoping to cash in on the price gains.
On average prices on key shares were stable with a few registering marginal gains as investors bought ahead of anticipated mainly financial year-end results.
Barclays Bank was unchanged at 120 while Standard Chartered Bank firmed to 57 from 56.50. Kenya Commercial Bank edged to 93.50 from 93.
Foreigners bought Uchumi at between 40 and 41.75 from 40 and Firestone East Africa at 30 unchanged.

Bamburi Cement announced a bonus issue of one share for every two shares held and a final dividend of 75 cents. The company posted a profit of 767 million shillings after tax for the year ended December 31 1996 compared to 682 million shillings in the previous year.
Rea Vipingo Plantations closed at 11.90 from 12.
